bull_bear.body: Intense competition in the auto components industry; Regulatory changes affecting the automotive sector
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's diversified product portfolio and strong relationships with major automotive OEMs provide a competitive advantage
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Business restructuring during FY 26: "the business of Castings & Sheet Metal was restructured into wholly owned subsidiaries during FY 26", which the deck flags makes previous and corresponding-quarter standalone figures not comparable.
- ₹341 Crs of investment is currently parked in four new India projects that are yet to achieve volumes and carry a PBT loss in the quarter, so near-term returns are pre-ramp.
- Capability expansion is split between wholly owned subsidiaries (castings, sheet metal, EV powertrain, after market) and joint ventures with Korean/Taiwanese partners for electronics and smart products, rather than a single-entity build.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Scale and spread of the manufacturing footprint - 44 manufacturing facilities and 14,000+ strength globally, with plants across eight Indian states and four overseas countries
- Product diversity across locking systems, mirrors, operator cabins, aluminium components and precision assemblies, so that no single product line dominates turnover (largest, Locks, is 26.79% of turnover)
- Backward integration - the Casting, Machining & Tooling operation supports internal requirements of key materials and processes for products manufactured by the automotive division
- Long-standing OEM relationships built since 1987, described as a customer-first approach with co-creation from leading OEMs to emerging EV platforms
- Strategic collaborations with global players in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan
- Balance-sheet standing recognised externally, with the credit rating reaffirmed at IND AA-/Stable during the year
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate change - physical and transition risk — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as both a risk and an opportunity with significant implications for long-term operational and financial sustainability: physical risks such as extreme weather events and supply chain disruptions, and transition risks such as evolving regulations and shifting market preferences. Mitigation is stated to sit inside the enterprise risk management framework - ongoing assessment and reduction of carbon footprint across operations and supply chain, adoption of cleaner technologies and energy-efficient manufacturing, and monitoring regulatory developments. Financial implications are marked 'Negative and Positive'.
- Technology disruption from electrification and the shift to new-age mobility — The Board's Report describes an industry undergoing significant transformation driven by increasing adoption of electric vehicles, technological advancements, digitalization and sustainability initiatives, with electric passenger vehicle registrations growing more than 80% in FY 2025-26 and EV components already about 4.6% of total supplies to OEMs per ACMA. For a legacy internal-combustion-era component supplier this is a structural re-tooling requirement; the BRSR frames the same shift as an opportunity through increased demand for sustainable mobility solutions.
- Geopolitical uncertainty feeding through to crude, commodity and freight costs — The Board's Report explicitly flags that the industry continues to operate in an environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties, particularly ongoing tensions in West Asia, which may impact crude oil prices, commodity costs, freight rates and global trade flows - all direct input-cost and logistics exposures for a metal-components manufacturer.
- Input-cost, foreign-exchange and supply-chain volatility — The Board's Report names volatility in fuel prices, foreign exchange fluctuations, supply chain disruptions, shipping route constraints and broader macroeconomic uncertainties as factors that may influence demand patterns, input costs and operational efficiencies across the automotive value chain. The Company has overseas plants and international sales, so currency and shipping exposure is structural rather than incidental.
- Dependence on the automotive demand cycle — The Company's fortunes are tied to a single end-industry: the Board's Report states the automotive component industry is 'closely linked to the Company's core business', and the Board's Report attributes the year to industry-level conditions, describing Financial Year 2025-26 as a landmark year for the Indian automobile industry as reported by SIAM. The same industry-level levers reverse in a downcycle.
- Waste management and hazardous-waste handling — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table: improper handling, treatment or disposal of waste can pose environmental, regulatory and reputational risks, and the Company acknowledges that being part of a resource-intensive manufacturing sector it generates various types of industrial and hazardous waste. The stated mitigation is limited to disposal of waste through authorised vendors.
- Water availability and water-use regulation — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table: water is a critical natural resource for manufacturing operations, and the Company recognises water scarcity, regulatory pressure and community expectations as key risks requiring proactive mitigation, with efficient management essential for business continuity and its licence to operate.
- Governance of risk is board-level but thinly evidenced in this bundle — A Risk Management Committee exists, chaired by Shri Sandeep Dinodia with Shri Vimal Mahendru, Smt. Aabha Bakaya and Smt. Monica Davar as members, and the BRSR refers to an enterprise risk management framework into which climate considerations are integrated. Beyond the BRSR material-issues rows and the Board's Report industry commentary, no separate 'Risks and Concerns' narrative quantifying exposures appears in this bundle.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- "Strategically Located Plants across all major auto hubs" with a global and domestic footprint: India 34 plants, Overseas 4 plants, JV 6 plants and 1 R&D Centre.
- Diversified customer-category exposure across 2W, 3W, 4W (PV & CV) and OHV (off-highway vehicles), so no single vehicle segment carries the whole portfolio.
- Technology access is structured through joint ventures with South Korean, Taiwanese and Indian partners (Sandhar Amkin, Sandhar Whetron Electronics, Sandhar Han Sung Technologies, Winnercom Sandhar Technologies, Sandhar Han Shin Auto Technologies), with the parent described as supplying "Technologically Advanced & Smart Products".
- Group is organised as a listed parent (Sandhar Technologies Ltd) plus wholly owned subsidiaries by capability — Ascast (aluminium & zinc die casting), Auto Castings (machining for casting), Engineering (sheet metal fabrication), Automotive Systems (B2C after market), Auto Electric Solutions (powertrain & EV) and Technologies Barcelona SL (aluminium die casting holding co.).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] The new-projects table lists an "SCL Acquired Business" at Hosur under Sandhar Ascast Pvt Ltd (ADC - HPDC & LPDC), with turnaround expected by Q4 FY-27; the deck gives no acquisition consideration or date.
- [Regulatory cost] Statutory minimum wage revisions in Haryana & Uttarakhand are called out as a distinct P&L impact (Rs. 5.84 Crs consolidated, Rs. 3.08 Crs standalone), indicating a recurring labour-cost step-up rather than a one-off.
- [Contradiction] The deck states two different PBT losses from new projects for the same quarter: Rs. 7.41 Crs (described as from new projects in India, on the Financial Summary slide and matching the New Projects table PBT of (-)7.41) and Rs. 4.81 Crs (in the Consolidated Financial Performance note). Both readings are reported as printed.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Sandhar has grown since 1987 from locking systems and mirrors into operator cabins, aluminium components and precision assemblies, describing itself in the BRSR as a market leader in the automotive components and system segment. Sales are primarily conducted through a Business-to-Business (B2B) model, catering mainly to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), with the entity's business activity classified entirely as manufacturing of Metal & Metal Products. The portfolio is organised around an Automotive Division, a Sheet Metal & Allied Business, a Cabins and Fabrication Division serving off-highway vehicles, and a Casting, Machining & Tooling operation that supports the automotive division's internal requirements.

outlook.body:
- Investing in Emerging Trends - investing in R&D, collaborations and technology-led initiatives to build differentiated solutions
- Scaling with Demand - expanding capacity through new facilities and enhanced operations to remain agile and responsive
- Expanding the product portfolio - innovating and diversifying offerings to serve growing needs across vehicle segments
- Deepening customer relationships - strengthening partnerships through performance, innovation, quality and value creation, working with leading OEMs and emerging EV platforms to co-create solutions
- Streamlining the portfolio around core business: divesting the entire stake in the Kwangsung Sandhar joint venture (KSTPL) and in KSTPL's subsidiary KSASPL to Kwangsung Corporation Ltd, stated to be in line with the objective to streamline operations, optimise resource allocation, enhance operational efficiency and strengthen focus on core business areas
- Consolidating the aluminium die-casting business under wholly owned subsidiary Sandhar Ascast Private Limited via slump sale of the Hosur (Tamil Nadu) Unit I and Bawal, Rewari (Haryana) Unit V undertakings, bringing new capability and scale into the portfolio
- Taking the business onto the global stage through Sandhar Technologies Barcelona S.L., extending presence into Europe and closer to demanding international customers
- Building the EV business toward profitability as electrification, smarter manufacturing and new mobility solutions reshape the industry
- Securing a long-term reliable source of renewable energy through Solar and Wind Power in Karnataka, via a Share Purchase Agreement with a captive-generating SPV
- Commitment to Atmanirbhar Bharat - supporting indigenous manufacturing, innovation, employment generation and sustainable industrial growth
- Sustainability pillars of Climate Conscious (lowering CO2 emissions, increasing renewable energy adoption), Resource Efficient (optimising raw material and energy use, minimising waste) and Quality & Compliance (aligning products and processes with global regulatory, safety and quality standards)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report frames expansion qualitatively rather than as a capex programme. Under 'Strategic Actions for Future Growth' the Company commits to 'Scaling with Demand - expanding capacity through new facilities and enhanced operations to remain agile and responsive', alongside investing in R&D, collaborations and technology-led initiatives, diversifying the product portfolio and deepening customer relationships. The footprint is described as 44 manufacturing facilities and 14,000+ strength globally, with plants in Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu in India and overseas plants in Romania, Poland, Mexico and Spain, plus strategic collaborations in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. The concrete structural moves of FY 2025-26, all in the Board's Report Major Highlights, are: (i) the slump sale of the Aluminium Die Casting business on a going-concern basis to wholly owned subsidiary Sandhar Ascast Private Limited - the Tamil Nadu Unit I at Hosur Taluk, Krishnagiri completed on 01st March 2026 and the Haryana Unit V at Bawal, Rewari completed on 01st February 2026; (ii) an additional equity investment of EUR 915,000 via rights issue into the equity share capital of Sandhar Technologies Barcelona S.L.; (iii) a Share Purchase Agreement with Clean Renewable Energy KK1A Private Limited (SPV) for an investment of INR 2,72,00,000 to secure a long-term reliable source of renewable energy through Solar and Wind Power in the State of Karnataka, sourced from a captive generating arrangement; and (iv) the sale of the entire stake in joint venture Kwangsung Sandhar Technologies Private Limited and its subsidiary KSASPL to Kwangsung Corporation Ltd, to streamline operations and sharpen focus on core business. No capacity additions in physical units, no project cost, and no commissioning timeline for any greenfield or brownfield line are disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects the Indian automotive industry to maintain a positive growth trajectory, supported by favourable demographics, increasing vehicle penetration, infrastructure development, technological advancements, and the transition towards sustainable mobility solutions
- As reported by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Financial Year 2025-26 was a landmark year for the Indian automobile industry, and the Passenger Vehicle segment moved from a marginal de-growth in the first half to double-digit growth in the second
- Demand was lifted in the second half by the GST 2.0 rate reduction effective from 22nd September 2025, combined with improved financing conditions, rising disposable incomes and sustained infrastructure investments - a strong H2 that more than offset a relatively subdued first half
- Electrification is a stated structural driver: registrations of electric passenger vehicles grew by more than 80% during Financial Year 2025-26, and electric vehicle components accounted for about 4.6% of total supplies to OEMs per ACMA
- The component industry, closely linked to the Company's core business, grew 6.8% in H1 FY 2025-26 to Rs 3.56 lakh crore per ACMA, with supplies to OEMs up 7.3%, the aftermarket up 9%, and component exports up 9.3% to USD 12.1 billion
- Export demand remained resilient across Africa, the Middle East, Latin America and neighbouring countries, with total vehicle exports from India crossing 66.48 lakh units, up 24%
- Margin lever: the Chairman notes core India operations grew strongly with margins expanding meaningfully, described as proof that existing businesses are getting stronger even as new ones are built
- Watch-items flagged: geopolitical uncertainties, particularly ongoing tensions in West Asia, which may impact crude oil prices, commodity costs, freight rates and global trade flows; plus volatility in fuel prices, foreign exchange fluctuations, supply chain disruptions and shipping route constraints
- Long-term demand themes cited in the corporate overview: changing demographics driving personal and commercial mobility demand, globalization, digital transformation raising demand for advanced integrated solutions, and the shift toward EVs and cleaner technologies

currentContext.expansion: The annual report frames expansion qualitatively rather than as a capex programme. Under 'Strategic Actions for Future Growth' the Company commits to 'Scaling with Demand - expanding capacity through new facilities and enhanced operations to remain agile and responsive', alongside investing in R&D, collaborations and technology-led initiatives, diversifying the product portfolio and deepening customer relationships. The footprint is described as 44 manufacturing facilities and 14,000+ strength globally, with plants in Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu in India and overseas plants in Romania, Poland, Mexico and Spain, plus strategic collaborations in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. The concrete structural moves of FY 2025-26, all in the Board's Report Major Highlights, are: (i) the slump sale of the Aluminium Die Casting business on a going-concern basis to wholly owned subsidiary Sandhar Ascast Private Limited - the Tamil Nadu Unit I at Hosur Taluk, Krishnagiri completed on 01st March 2026 and the Haryana Unit V at Bawal, Rewari completed on 01st February 2026; (ii) an additional equity investment of EUR 915,000 via rights issue into the equity share capital of Sandhar Technologies Barcelona S.L.; (iii) a Share Purchase Agreement with Clean Renewable Energy KK1A Private Limited (SPV) for an investment of INR 2,72,00,000 to secure a long-term reliable source of renewable energy through Solar and Wind Power in the State of Karnataka, sourced from a captive generating arrangement; and (iv) the sale of the entire stake in joint venture Kwangsung Sandhar Technologies Private Limited and its subsidiary KSASPL to Kwangsung Corporation Ltd, to streamline operations and sharpen focus on core business. No capacity additions in physical units, no project cost, and no commissioning timeline for any greenfield or brownfield line are disclosed in this bundle.

risks.risk: Climate change - physical and transition risk
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as both a risk and an opportunity with significant implications for long-term operational and financial sustainability: physical risks such as extreme weather events and supply chain disruptions, and transition risks such as evolving regulations and shifting market preferences. Mitigation is stated to sit inside the enterprise risk management framework - ongoing assessment and reduction of carbon footprint across operations and supply chain, adoption of cleaner technologies and energy-efficient manufacturing, and monitoring regulatory developments. Financial implications are marked 'Negative and Positive'.

risks.risk: Technology disruption from electrification and the shift to new-age mobility
risks.note: The Board's Report describes an industry undergoing significant transformation driven by increasing adoption of electric vehicles, technological advancements, digitalization and sustainability initiatives, with electric passenger vehicle registrations growing more than 80% in FY 2025-26 and EV components already about 4.6% of total supplies to OEMs per ACMA. For a legacy internal-combustion-era component supplier this is a structural re-tooling requirement; the BRSR frames the same shift as an opportunity through increased demand for sustainable mobility solutions.

risks.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty feeding through to crude, commodity and freight costs
risks.note: The Board's Report explicitly flags that the industry continues to operate in an environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties, particularly ongoing tensions in West Asia, which may impact crude oil prices, commodity costs, freight rates and global trade flows - all direct input-cost and logistics exposures for a metal-components manufacturer.

The Board's Report names volatility in fuel prices, foreign exchange fluctuations, supply chain disruptions, shipping route constraints and broader macroeconomic uncertainties as factors that may influence demand patterns, input costs and operational efficiencies across the automotive value chain. The Company has overseas plants and international sales, so currency and shipping exposure is structural rather than incidental.

risks.risk: Dependence on the automotive demand cycle
risks.note: The Company's fortunes are tied to a single end-industry: the Board's Report states the automotive component industry is 'closely linked to the Company's core business', and the Board's Report attributes the year to industry-level conditions, describing Financial Year 2025-26 as a landmark year for the Indian automobile industry as reported by SIAM. The same industry-level levers reverse in a downcycle.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table: improper handling, treatment or disposal of waste can pose environmental, regulatory and reputational risks, and the Company acknowledges that being part of a resource-intensive manufacturing sector it generates various types of industrial and hazardous waste. The stated mitigation is limited to disposal of waste through authorised vendors.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table: water is a critical natural resource for manufacturing operations, and the Company recognises water scarcity, regulatory pressure and community expectations as key risks requiring proactive mitigation, with efficient management essential for business continuity and its licence to operate.

risks.risk: Governance of risk is board-level but thinly evidenced in this bundle
risks.note: A Risk Management Committee exists, chaired by Shri Sandeep Dinodia with Shri Vimal Mahendru, Smt. Aabha Bakaya and Smt. Monica Davar as members, and the BRSR refers to an enterprise risk management framework into which climate considerations are integrated. Beyond the BRSR material-issues rows and the Board's Report industry commentary, no separate 'Risks and Concerns' narrative quantifying exposures appears in this bundle.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects the Indian automotive industry to maintain a positive growth trajectory, supported by favourable demographics, increasing vehicle penetration, infrastructure development, technological advancements, and the transition towards sustainable mobility solutions
- As reported by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Financial Year 2025-26 was a landmark year for the Indian automobile industry, and the Passenger Vehicle segment moved from a marginal de-growth in the first half to double-digit growth in the second
- Demand was lifted in the second half by the GST 2.0 rate reduction effective from 22nd September 2025, combined with improved financing conditions, rising disposable incomes and sustained infrastructure investments - a strong H2 that more than offset a relatively subdued first half
- Electrification is a stated structural driver: registrations of electric passenger vehicles grew by more than 80% during Financial Year 2025-26, and electric vehicle components accounted for about 4.6% of total supplies to OEMs per ACMA
- The component industry, closely linked to the Company's core business, grew 6.8% in H1 FY 2025-26 to Rs 3.56 lakh crore per ACMA, with supplies to OEMs up 7.3%, the aftermarket up 9%, and component exports up 9.3% to USD 12.1 billion
- Export demand remained resilient across Africa, the Middle East, Latin America and neighbouring countries, with total vehicle exports from India crossing 66.48 lakh units, up 24%
- Margin lever: the Chairman notes core India operations grew strongly with margins expanding meaningfully, described as proof that existing businesses are getting stronger even as new ones are built
- Watch-items flagged: geopolitical uncertainties, particularly ongoing tensions in West Asia, which may impact crude oil prices, commodity costs, freight rates and global trade flows; plus volatility in fuel prices, foreign exchange fluctuations, supply chain disruptions and shipping route constraints
- Long-term demand themes cited in the corporate overview: changing demographics driving personal and commercial mobility demand, globalization, digital transformation raising demand for advanced integrated solutions, and the shift toward EVs and cleaner technologies

The concrete structural moves of FY 2025-26, all in the Board's Report Major Highlights, are: (i) the slump sale of the Aluminium Die Casting business on a going-concern basis to wholly owned subsidiary Sandhar Ascast Private Limited - the Tamil Nadu Unit I at Hosur Taluk, Krishnagiri completed on 01st March 2026 and the Haryana Unit V at Bawal, Rewari completed on 01st February 2026; (ii) an additional equity investment of EUR 915,000 via rights issue into the equity share capital of Sandhar Technologies Barcelona S.L.; (iii) a Share Purchase Agreement with Clean Renewable Energy KK1A Private Limited (SPV) for an investment of INR 2,72,00,000 to secure a long-term reliable source of renewable energy through Solar and Wind Power in the State of Karnataka, sourced from a captive generating arrangement; and (iv) the sale of the entire stake in joint venture Kwangsung Sandhar Technologies Private Limited and its subsidiary KSASPL to Kwangsung Corporation Ltd, to streamline operations and sharpen focus on core business. themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
